qualifications: The exponent h(t) is finite and nonnegative. There is a computable function T such that h(t) ≤ max(1, t log₂(max(2, t)))/j for every positive integer j and every t ≥ T(j).

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides Vertex-Disjoint Paths within the stated running time.

encoding: A finite simple undirected graph G and an explicit list of demand pairs of vertices.

inputConditions.condition: The graph is connected and bipartite, and its maximum degree is at most three.
All demand endpoints are distinct leaves.
The treewidth and pathwidth of G are equal.

parameter: The intrinsic treewidth t of G.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: SH excludes each fixed power below one in the exponent. The ETH benchmark excludes every little-o exponent at the larger logarithmically superlinear scale.

evidence.locator: Table 1, Disjoint Paths row and footnote d, p. 4, and Theorem 3.1, p. 8

recoveryAssessments.comparison: The recovery excludes the same scale with a computable convergence modulus. The proof obtains the exclusion on connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree three with distinct leaf terminals and equal widths.

task: Is there one path joining the endpoints of each demand pair, with all the paths pairwise vertex-disjoint?
title: Vertex-Disjoint Paths by treewidth
